excerpt: You built one of Africa’s most prosperous nations from cane fields and an open port, and you hold reserves worth about two thirds of a year’s output.
paras: You built one of Africa’s most prosperous nations from cane fields and an open port, and you hold reserves worth about two thirds of a year’s output. Your debt is high, and you have written its limit into law. Let your institutions, your reserves and your ocean carry capital at the price they deserve.

Your partners are investing in your islands. In 2023 the World Bank approved $184 million for a new airport on Rodrigues. The Special Economic Package agreed with India in September 2025 brings about $440 million of grants and credit for roads, the airport and the port, and $215 million more in grants. In April 2025 the French Development Agency lent €45 million and €38.5 million, backed by the Green Climate Fund, to two of your banks for green investment.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. Forty-nine in every hundred of your city dwellers live in slums, on the United Nations measure. At the last count, in 2006, forty in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text. Twenty-eight in every hundred of you cannot always count on enough good food. Shelter sets your Coverage today, at 51.3 out of 100, with reading and food close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Mauritius: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Mauritian falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: You wrote the limit into law. Let the markets read it, and price it.
